question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-z&=4 \\ x+3y&=5 \\ x+2y-3z&=8\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-6y&=-9 \\ 2x-3y+z&=-2 \\ -2x+5y+2z&=11\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -6 & 0 & -9 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 5 & 2 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 5\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y&=-3 \\ y+z&=4 \\ z&=1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=1 \\ y&=4-(1)(1)=3 \\ x&=-3-(-2)(3)-(0)(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,3,1\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ -1 & -3 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -4\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z&=1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(0)(4)=-3 \\ x&=1-(2)(-3)-(1)(4)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 3,-3,4\rangle$.

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{2}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -8\end{array}\right].

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{array}\right].

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+z&=1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=4\end{aligned}\right..

\begin{aligned}z&=4 \\ y&=-3-(0)(4)=-3 \\ x&=1-(2)(-3)-(1)(4)=3.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2z&=-1 \\ y&=-3 \\ z&=-1\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-1 \\ y&=-3-(0)(-1)=-3 \\ x&=-1-(0)(-3)-(-2)(-1)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -3,-3,-1\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-2 \\ x+2y+z &=-1 \\ x+3y+z &=-5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=1 \\ y &=-3-(1)(1) \\ &=-4 \\ x &=-2-(2)(-4) \\ &\quad -(0)(1) \\ &=6\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(6,-4,1\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+2y-4z &=6 \\ -2x-2y+7z &=3 \\ -3y+6z &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 2 & -4 & 6 \\ -2 & -2 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 2 & -2 & -4 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & 2 & -2 & -4 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 4 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=1 \\ y &=-3-(2)(1) \\ &=-5 \\ x &=-2-(1)(-5) \\ &\quad -(-1)(1) \\ &=4\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(4,-5,1\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-3y &=0 \\ -2x+2y-3z &=0 \\ 2x-5y-4z &=-5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}3 & -3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{3}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -5 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-2)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & -5\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=0 \\ y &=\frac{5}{3}-\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)(0) \\ &=\frac{5}{3} \\ x &=0-(-1)\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &\quad -(0)(0) \\ &=\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},0\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}2 & -6 & 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1:=\frac{1}{2}R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -5 & 3 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 1 & -6 & -3 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -3 & -5 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize with $R_3:=-\frac{1}{3}R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{3} & -\frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{5}{3}\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=-\frac{5}{3} \\ y &=-\frac{1}{3}-\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{22}{9} \\ x &=2-(-3)\left(\frac{22}{9}\right) \\ &\quad -(2)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{38}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(\frac{38}{3},\frac{22}{9},-\frac{5}{3}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-3x-9y+3z &=3 \\ x+3y+z &=-5 \\ -2x-3y &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-3 & -9 & 3 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 & -5 \\ -2 & -3 & 0 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y+6z &=5 \\ y-10z &=-11 \\ 4x+8y+13z &=9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 4 & 8 & 13 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & -11 & -11\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=-\frac{1}{11}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -10 & -11 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-4y+4z&=2 \\ x-y+4z&=-10 \\ 2x+6y-5z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -4 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 4 & -10 \\ 2 & 6 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 4 & -10 \\ 2 & 6 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & -9 \\ 2 & 6 & -5 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 6 & -9 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=-\frac{1}{3}R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{3}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y-2z&=-1 \\ y-2z&=3 \\ z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-2 \\ y&=3-(-2)(-2)=-1 \\ x&=-1-(2)(-1)-(-2)(-2)=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -3,-1,-2\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{7}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{7}\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$
